entries.title: Draft boundary example: bounded degree does not imply critical extinction
entries.statement: Independent review pending. Let T be the rooted tree in which each vertex at level n-1 has 8 children if n is a power of two and 2 children otherwise, for n>=1. T is infinite, connected, simple and locally finite, with maximum degree 9. For iid Bernoulli bond percolation, p_c(T)=1/2 and the root survives at criticality with probability at least 4/5. At p=1/2 the open generation mean is M_n=4^(1+floor(log_2 n)), and its normalized second moment is 1+(1/2)sum_{j<=n}1/M_j<=5/4. Two independent uniform-child rays on the host have E[2^K]=5/4, where K counts their common undirected edges. Below 1/2, M_n<=4n^2(2p)^n tends to zero. The degree-8 root is unique, so every automorphism fixes it and T has infinitely many vertex orbits. This example excludes replacing quasi-transitivity by bounded degree; it does not refute critical extinction on quasi-transitive graphs.
assumptions: The exact dyadic offspring schedule stated here

entries.title: Draft thinning fact: surviving critical components have threshold one
entries.statement: Independent review pending. Let G be a countable connected locally finite graph with p_c(G)>0 and sample iid Bernoulli bond percolation at p_c(G). Almost surely every infinite open component C, regarded as a fixed graph after conditioning on the sampled field, has quenched bond threshold p_c(C)=1. For rational r<1, independent r-thinning of the sampled open bonds is unconditionally iid bond percolation at p_c(G)r<p_c(G), so its probability of any infinite component is zero. Conditioning, then intersecting over rational r and using monotonicity, proves simultaneous failure of percolation below r=1 on every C. Infinitude of C alone therefore supplies no robustness under thinning.
assumptions: G countable, connected and locally finite
Independent bond retention and independent subsequent thinning

entries.title: Draft refuted inference: host ray energy passes to critical clusters
entries.statement: Independent review pending. The proposed implication 'finite common-edge ray energy on a host graph implies that a surviving critical component inherits finite ray energy at some thinning retention r<1' is false without an additional structural premise. For two independent rays from a Borel ray measure mu write I_r(mu)=E[r^(-K)], where K counts common undirected edges. On the dyadic-burst tree, the uniform-child host measure has I_(1/2)=5/4 and critical root survival probability is at least 4/5. Nevertheless almost surely every infinite critical component C has p_c(C)=1. Such C admits no ray measure with finite I_r for r<1: the open-prefix second-moment argument would give positive percolation probability at r, a contradiction. The host is not quasi-transitive; this refutes unconditional inheritance and leaves a quasi-transitive structural premise unproved.
assumptions: The dyadic-burst tree defined in this bundle
Ray measures are on infinite simple rays of the graph in question
Independent critical percolation and independent thinning

relations.rationale: The first endpoint supplies an explicit host with finite ray energy and positive critical survival; the third endpoint states the false unconditional inheritance implication and identifies its failure on that same host.
Threshold one of every surviving critical component, combined with the open-prefix ray-energy sufficient condition, excludes finite energy for every retention below one.

Both endpoints concern infinite clusters at the critical parameter. The new example tests why the quasi-transitive hypothesis in the existing conjecture cannot simply be replaced by bounded degree; its graph explicitly lies outside that hypothesis and does not refute the conjecture.
